transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I need help dealing with the people who are monitoring me. There is an organization that has been watching my apartment and tracking my movements wherever I go. I just don't know how to make them stop.
Have you been experiencing any unusual mood swings, such as feelings of extreme happiness or sadness, or have you been feeling depressed or anxious most of the time?
No, I haven't really experienced any extreme mood swings, depression, or anxiety. My mood is generally fine, aside from just feeling stressed about the people who are monitoring me.
Have you been hearing any voices or sounds that other people can't hear, or seeing things that aren't really there, aside from the people you believe are monitoring you?
No, I don't hear any voices or see things that aren't there. My hearing and sight are perfectly fine, and everything I see is completely real.
How long have you believed that this organization is monitoring you, and has your belief about being monitored been consistent over time?
This has been going on for about two years now, and it has been completely constant. My belief hasn't wavered for a single day because I know without a doubt they are always watching me.

Aside from the stress caused by the monitoring, has your daily life, such as work, relationships, or social activities, been significantly impacted by your beliefs or have you been able to maintain relatively normal functioning?

Aside from the constant stress, I've been able to keep up with my normal routine. I still go to work every day and manage my responsibilities just fine, even though I have to be careful. My daily life is mostly normal, it's just very exhausting having to deal with this situation all the time.
Can you tell me more about the organization you believe is monitoring you, such as what you think their goals are or why you think they are specifically targeting you?

It is hard to say exactly what their ultimate goals are, but I can constantly feel them watching and targeting me. The constant pressure of being under their lens is just incredibly exhausting and causes me a lot of unease. It has been really difficult to relax lately because of how much this situation is weighing on my mind.
Do you think your beliefs about being monitored could possibly be mistaken, or do you believe them to be absolute facts?

These are absolute facts, and there is no mistake about it. I know for a certainty that I am being monitored, and it is definitely not just in my head. It is frustrating to even have it suggested that I might be imagining this when I have to live through it every single day.

latest_inference.note: The patient's consistent and persistent belief in being monitored by an organization, without any evidence of hallucinations or significant impact on daily functioning aside from the stress caused by the delusion, supports Delusional Disorder as the primary candidate. Schizophrenia is less likely due to the absence of hallucinations, disorganized speech, or significant negative symptoms, and the patient's ability to maintain relatively normal functioning. The patient's delusion is non-bizarre (involving situations that occur in real life, such as being followed) and has been present for more than a month, which further aligns with the criteria for Delusional Disorder. The patient's denial of any extreme mood swings or depressive/anxious episodes also reduces the likelihood of other disorders such as Schizoaffective Disorder or Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features. Therefore, Delusional Disorder remains as the most fitting diagnosis based on the information provided.
